briefdescription.para: Mark the beginning of a test session.

detaileddescription.para:
runner
Reference to the test runner.
Returns
Nothing.
If verbosity is not silent, a blank line is printed to stdout before the build-information block emitted by write_info_(). A fixed "µTest++ human report" heading is then written to the output file (if open) and, unless verbosity is silent, to stdout. The add_empty_line_ flag is set so that subsequent suite output is visually separated.

briefdescription.para: Mark the beginning of a subtest.

detaileddescription.para:
subtest
Reference to the subtest.
Returns
Nothing.
This method marks the beginning of a test case. The output buffer must be empty at this point; if it is not, its content is written to stderr and execution is aborted.
A "• <name>" line, indented according to the nesting depth, is written to the output file (if open) and, with verbose verbosity, to stdout, preceded by an empty line when add_empty_line_ is set.

briefdescription.para: Mark the beginning of a suite.

detaileddescription.para:
suite
Reference to the suite.
Returns
Nothing.
With normal or verbose verbosity, this method writes a "• <name>" line, marking the beginning of the test suite, to the output file (if open) and to stdout, preceded on stdout by an empty line when add_empty_line_ is set. For silent or quiet verbosity levels, no output is produced.

briefdescription.para: Mark the end of a test session.

detaileddescription.para:
runner
Reference to the test runner.
Returns
Nothing.
Unless verbosity is silent, prints a summary line to stdout (and to the output file if open) showing the total number of successful checks, failed checks, executed test cases, and test suites, together with the elapsed time when timing data is available. The line is prefixed with a green ✓ tick on success or a red ✗ cross on failure, using ANSI colour codes when colour output is enabled.

briefdescription.para: Mark the end of a subtest.

detaileddescription.para:
subtest
Reference to the subtest.
Returns
Nothing.
With normal or verbose verbosity, this method summarises the outcome of the test case, with appropriate formatting and colour coding; for silent or quiet verbosity levels, no output is produced.

For passing test cases, a "✓ <name> - passed" line is shown with the number of checks; the buffered check results are written to stdout only with verbose verbosity. For failing test cases, the buffered check results are always shown (preceded, with normal verbosity, by the test case name), followed by a "✗ <name> - FAILED" line with the number of successful and failed checks. The buffered results are always written to the output file.
Finally, the streams are flushed and the buffer is cleared.

briefdescription.para: Mark the end of a test suite.

detaileddescription.para:
suite
Reference to the test suite.
Returns
Nothing.
With normal or verbose verbosity, this method summarises the results of the test suite, with appropriate formatting and colour coding; for silent or quiet verbosity levels, no output is produced. An empty line is first added if the suite executed any test cases.

For suites without failed checks, a "✓ <name> - passed" line is displayed, including the number of checks and test cases; the buffered check results are written to stdout only with verbose verbosity. Otherwise, a "✗ <name> - FAILED" line is shown, detailing the number of successful and failed checks and the number of test cases, preceded by the buffered check results. The buffered results are always written to the output file. The elapsed time is appended when available.
Finally, the streams are flushed and the buffer is cleared.

briefdescription.para: Inserts a line ending into the output buffer and flushes the output streams.

detaileddescription.para:
Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
This method appends a newline character to the internal output buffer of the reporter and calls flush(). The buffer itself is written later, by the concrete reporters, at the end of each subtest or suite.

This allows the reporter to delegate the formatting of complex expressions to the expression_formatter, which provides a consistent and extensible way to convert various types of values and expressions into their string representations for output in test reports.

briefdescription.para: Output operator to display any pointer.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The type of the pointer.
v
The pointer value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload enables the reporter to output pointer values in a consistent and readable format.
Null pointers are always rendered as the string "0x0", regardless of the platform, avoiding platform-specific representations such as "(nil)" on Linux/glibc.

Non-null pointers are formatted as a hexadecimal address using snprintf with the p format specifier. The resulting string is appended to the internal output buffer, allowing pointer values to be included in test reports and diagnostics.
This approach provides clear and unambiguous representation of pointer addresses, which is particularly useful for debugging and verifying pointer-related test cases.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for arithmetic types.

detaileddescription.para:

v
The value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This template operator overload allows the reporter to output values of any arithmetic type (integral or floating-point) in a consistent and readable format. The value is formatted using the detail::append_number_() helper, without a type suffix (unlike the detail::expression_formatter operators, which add one).

This method outputs the prefix for a failing check result, indented one level deeper than the subtest. The prefix includes a cross symbol (✗), an optional message, and the label "FAILED", both symbol and label in the fail colour. briefdescription.para: Output the current buffered content to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: The buffer is written without appending a line ending, and is not cleared. ANSI colour sequences are removed, so the file receives plain text even when the console output is coloured. If no output file is open, the call has no effect.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Writes the contents of buffer_ to output_file_ without appending a newline. If output_file_ is null, the call is a no-op.

The buffer may contain ANSI colour sequences, added when the console is a terminal, which must not reach the file. They are removed while writing: each ESC [, followed by any digits and semicolons, and terminated by m, is skipped, and the text between the sequences is written unchanged. Any other use of ESC is written as is.

briefdescription.para: Write formatted text to the console.

detaileddescription.para: All reporter console output is routed through this function, so that it reaches the standard output stream via a single path, shared with the output of the user printf() calls. Using one stream-based path keeps the reporter and user output in the same buffer, preserving their relative order.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on stdout. The stream is explicit, so the compiler does not rewrite the call into puts() or putchar(), and all console output shares the same FILE-based path.

briefdescription.para: Write formatted text to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: If no output file is open, the call has no effect, so callers do not need to check output_file_ themselves.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on output_file_. If output_file_ is null, the arguments are ignored.

briefdescription.para: Writes the informational (non-result) lines to the console and to the output file.

detaileddescription.para:
Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Constructs and emits two informational lines, each prefixed by get_comment_prefix(): the first lists the program name (without the path) and any command-line arguments; the second identifies the compiler (Clang, GCC, or MSVC) together with the version string, floating-point availability on bare-metal targets, exception support, and any active debug or trace macros. Both lines are written to the output file when one is open, and to stdout when the verbosity is normal or verbose, except when both MICRO_OS_PLUS_STARTUP_ENABLED and MICRO_OS_PLUS_DIAG_TRACE_ENABLED are defined, since the startup code already displays this information.

briefdescription.para: Human (standard output) implementation of reporter.

detaileddescription.para: reporter_human provides a concrete implementation of the reporter abstract interface, formatting and presenting test results in a human-readable form. It accumulates output in an internal string buffer and writes it to the standard output stream, supporting colour-coded diagnostics (when the output is a terminal) and multiple verbosity levels.

The reporter is created by the runner, as selected by the --reporter command-line option. A different output format requires a new class derived from reporter, and an extension of the runner to create it.
All members and methods are defined within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.
